questions.question: The Article of the Indian Constitution that deals with all the executive powers of the Governor is ________.
questions.solution:
Article 154 states that the executive power of the State shall be vested in the Governor and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
  • Article 156: Deals with the term of office of the Governor.
  • Article 157: Deals with qualifications for appointment as Governor.

questions.question: In the absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, who presides the joint sitting of the two houses of Parliament?
questions.option_1: Any senior member of Lok Sabha
questions.option_2: Any senior member of Rajya Sabha
questions.solution:
If both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides over the joint sitting.
  • Prohibition: The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) never presides over a joint sitting because he is not a member of either House of Parliament.

questions.question: “The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them”. This has been incorporated in:
questions.solution:
The prohibition of discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth is incorporated in Article 15.
  • Note: This article is one of the Fundamental Rights available only to citizens of India.

questions.question: In the case of Mohammad Salimullah vs ________, the Supreme Court observed in 2021 that the 'Right not to be deported' is concomitant to Article 19 and available only to Indian citizens?
questions.solution:
In Mohammad Salimullah vs. Union of India (2021), the SC ruled that the right not to be deported is part of the right to reside and settle (Article 19), which is available only to Indian citizens, not illegal immigrants.
  • Context: This case specifically concerned the deportation of Rohingya refugees.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT a part of the Union Executive?
questions.solution:
The Supreme Court of India is part of the Judiciary, not the Union Executive.
  • Union Executive: Consists of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “Supreme Court to be a court of record”?
questions.solution:
Article 129 declares the Supreme Court to be a 'Court of Record'.
  • Implication: Its proceedings and acts are recorded for perpetual memory/testimony, and it has the power to punish for contempt of itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest High Court?
questions.solution:
The Calcutta High Court is the oldest High Court in India, established in July 1862.
  • Followed by: Bombay (August 1862) and Madras (August 1862).

questions.question: How many members of the Legislative Council are there in the state of Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The Karnataka Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) has 75 members.
  • Bicameral States: Karnataka is one of the few Indian states with a bicameral legislature (both Assembly and Council).

questions.question: How many types of writs can be issued by the Supreme Court of India for the protection of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The Supreme Court can issue five types of writs under Article 32: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.
  • Purpose: These are the tools used to enforce Fundamental Rights when they are violated.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
All India Services (IAS, IPS, IFoS) is a Unitary feature, not a federal one.
  • Reason: These officers are recruited by the Centre but serve the States, which gives the Union control over the State administration.
  • Federal Features: Written Constitution, Division of Powers, and Dual Government (Centre/State).

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.solution:
Part XIV (Articles 315 to 323) provides for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions.
  • Independence: This part ensures the commissions function independently of executive pressure.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Executive?
questions.solution:
Articles 52 to 78 in Part V deal with the Union Executive.
  • Article 52: Starts with the President of India.
  • Article 78: Ends with the duties of the Prime Minister regarding furnishing of information to the President.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
questions.option_2: To uphold and protect the unity and integrity of India
questions.solution:
To cast vote during elections is a legal/constitutional right (Article 326), but it is NOT listed as a Fundamental Duty in Article 51A.
  • Duties include: Protecting the environment, upholding integrity, and abiding by the Constitution.

questions.question: How many seats of Rajya Sabha are present in the state of Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The state of Maharashtra has 19 seats in the Rajya Sabha.
  • Context: It has the second-highest number of seats after Uttar Pradesh (31).

questions.question: A Minister who for any period of ______ is not a member of either House of Parliament shall at the expiration of that period cease to be a Minister.
questions.solution:
A person can remain a Minister for six consecutive months without being a member of either House.
  • Requirement: Before the expiry of 6 months, they must get elected to either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, or they must resign.

questions.question: Who termed Article 32 as the ‘heart and soul of the Constitution of India’?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar termed Article 32 as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'.
  • Reason: Without a remedy (the right to go to court), all other Fundamental Rights are just words on paper.

questions.question: To whom can the Judge of the Supreme Court address his/her resignation letter?
questions.solution:
A Judge of the Supreme Court addresses his/her resignation letter to the President of India.
  • Appointment: Since the President is the appointing authority, they are also the authority to receive the resignation.

questions.question: The Chairman of the Legislative Council is:
questions.option_1: elected by the Chief Minister and their Cabinet
questions.option_2: appointed by the Governor of that state
questions.option_3: appointed by the Chief Minister of that state
questions.option_4: elected by the members of the Legislative Council
questions.solution:
The Chairman of the Legislative Council is elected by the members of the Council from amongst themselves.
  • Contrast: In the Rajya Sabha, the Chairman is the Vice-President (ex-officio), not a member elected by the house.

questions.question: The election of the next Vice-President is to be held within _____ of the expiry of the term of office of the outgoing Vice-President.
questions.solution:
The election of a new Vice-President must be held within 60 days of the expiry of the term of the outgoing Vice-President.
  • Article 68: This ensures there is no prolonged vacancy in the office of the VP.
